::: {.education-intro}
::: {.education-copy}
These resources use water observations and other environmental datasets to teach scientific interpretation.

The SERC resources are short teaching activities; the HydroLearn resource is a longer course module. Follow each provider's instructions for access and classroom use.
:::

::: {.education-resources}

::: {.education-resource}
## Brine disposal and water quality

::: {.resource-meta}
**Undergraduate hydrology**\
2–3 hours · SERC
:::

Compare stream chemistry near brine-disposal locations and examine questions about wastewater disposal and seismicity. Created by Tao Wen.

[Explore the brine activity](env-brine.qmd){.resource-link}
:::

::: {.education-resource}
## Investigating methane in streams

::: {.resource-meta}
**Undergraduate hydrology**\
About 2 hours · SERC
:::

Work through three hypothetical water-supply investigations using stream observations and oil and gas records. The activity asks students to consider different potential methane sources.

[Explore the methane activity](env-methane.qmd){.resource-link}
:::

::: {.education-resource}
## Data science in Earth and environmental sciences

::: {.resource-meta}
**R and Python**\
About 30 hours · HydroLearn
:::

Practice programming and develop an environmental data-analysis workflow. Examples address wildfire and groundwater quality. Created by Tao Wen, Christina Bandaragoda, and Lucas Harris.

[Course details and access requirements](hydrolearn-ds-ees.qmd){.resource-link}
:::

:::

## Using these resources in a class

Review the activities and check their external tools before teaching; data interfaces can change. For questions about Shale Network data or adapting an activity, contact [Tao Wen](mailto:twen08@syr.edu).
